homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field; the homonyms are T's and the cards': PROV Exam (B2; T1-4, a map panel, Sandy, Utah, licensing exams) and PROV, a skate and streetwear shop in Jingumae, Shibuya, Tokyo (B5 its online store, B6 its Google place listing; T1-3, a map panel). They share the four letters PROV and no relation to the repository (CAP-1-06); card 5's title 'PROV ONLINE STORE' carries both 'PROV' and 'store', the two halves of the query string. They are other entities that share the letters, never senses of the name. The Capture Registry states that the record 'is to carry them as negative tags' (CAP-1-07); the census row does not (PE-13 is its only negative tag). In the archive, two string collisions met the traversal: 'OPM' is also the archive's Operative Philology Marks (#127), and 'provenance document' is also the archive's own genre of heteronym provenance documents (#90, #994, #1695), distinct from ProvStore's unit, a W3C PROV document.
distinct_entities: OpenProvenance (the operator; openprovenance.org, also served at openprovenance.sussex.ac.uk; its validator, translator and libraries)
W3C PROV (the standard ProvStore implements; PROV-DM, PROV-O, PROV-N, PROV Constraints; the W3C Provenance Working Group)
the Open Provenance Model (OPM; the predecessor model the composition joins into the repository's name)
the PROV Python package (the maintainer's library, begun 2012)
the Data Provenance Initiative (#725 lists it beside W3C PROV in the licensing dimension; /non row datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/data-provenance-explorer.json)

captures.description: PROVSTORE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'ProvStore most commonly refers to the Open Provenance Model / W3C PROV Public Repository, an online public provenance repository designed to store, browse, visualize, and manage data provenance documents using W3C standards via a web interface or REST API.' Then two local businesses with map panels: PROV Tokyo, a skate and streetwear shop in Shibuya (3.8, 50 reviews, 'Closed'), and the PROV Exam Bookstore in Sandy, Utah (4.2, 1.2K, 'Open'). The closing question offers the three. Six cards: the OpenProvenance page ('ProvStore is coming back soon'), PROV Exam, ePrints Soton and the ACM Digital Library (the paper), the PROV online store, a Google place listing.
